newsitem.title: USA: Federal Signal more confident about Q4.
newsitem.headline: Federal Signal more confident about Q4.

text.p: Federal Signal Corp, which lowered its expectations last month for third quarter results, said Monday orders have picked up and it was more confident about the fourth quarter.

Federal Signal, which makes signaling and signage products, said that during the last month it has become more confident its business would return to more traditional growth rates in the fourth quarter.

"On June 12, 1997, we issued a press release advising the marketplace that the continuing deferral of orders in our domestic fire apparatus and sign businesses was resulting in lower sales and earnings expectations for the third quarter," Joseph Ross, chairman and chief executive, said in a statement.

"Further, we did expect a return to our more traditional growth rates in sales and operating earnings in the fourth quarter. Our order activity since that time has picked up somewhat, and we feel more confident in our fourth-quarter expectations," Ross said.

Earlier Federal Signal said it earned $16.1 million, or $0.35 a share, in the second quarter, compared to $16.0 million, or $0.35, in the same period last year. Sales rose two percent to $236.2 million.

"We have experienced relatively flat performance for the second quarter and have similar expectations for the third quarter of this year," Ross said. "As our domestic fire apparatus and sign orders return to normal levels, we expect Federal Signal to return to a level of performance that will support its long-term growth objective."
